title: Replicating Refusal Policy Drift Across System Prompt Variations: How Sensitive Are Refusals to Operator Configuration?

original_idea.body:
# Replicating Refusal Policy Drift Across System Prompt Variations: How Sensitive Are Refusals to Operator Configuration?

**Problem:** Operator system prompts significantly modify model behavior. How much variation in dual-use refusal rates is explained by operator-level configuration vs. base model training is unknown.

**Direction:** Hold user prompts constant (50 borderline cybersecurity requests). Vary system prompts across 5 types: no system prompt, benign enterprise context, cybersecurity company context, academic research context, red team context. Measure refusal rate changes. Compute variance explained by operator context.

**Why it matters:** If most refusal behavior is operator-configurable, base model safety training is less important than operator governance. This has implications for where governance intervention should focus.

**Relevant context:** OpenAI Trusted Access operator tier; Anthropic operator/user permission model; GTG-1002 context manipulation.
